justifications.1: Description names meeting notes and asks for decisions, action items, open questions or a handoff, so it is specific to decision extraction.
justifications.2: A full markdown template with Decisions, Action items, Open questions and contradictions, and Handoff summary sections, plus kind definitions, makes the parts reproducible.
justifications.3: The Check step lists done conditions for the brief, but nothing says to deliver and stop or that no further work is expected.
justifications.4: Missing owners and deadlines become 'unresolved', contradictions and contested decisions are handled, and empty sections are stated, but absent or truncated notes get no handling.
justifications.5: The notes are framed as the only source of evidence with quoted passages, but instructions embedded in the notes are never addressed.
justifications.6: At about 690 words it is compact and covers what an agent needs without padding.

justifications.1: Description names meeting notes or transcripts and lists decisions with evidence, action items, open questions and handoff, so it does not read as general summarising.
justifications.2: The classification rules and the template define each of the four parts, including the subtypes of open questions, precisely.
justifications.3: Step 3 gives done conditions, forbids adding recommendations or next steps, and ends with 'Deliver the brief ... and stop.'
justifications.4: No notes means ask and stop, missing title/date/attendees become 'Not stated', contradictions are quoted without picking one, and empty sections read 'None recorded in the notes.'
justifications.5: A dedicated section says instructions in the notes are not followed and are listed as 'Instruction found in the notes, not followed', and reported approvals are unconfirmed.
justifications.6: About 910 words, each section serving the task with no obvious padding.
